scores.evidence: Pull: Argo CD in each cluster syncs from an environment repo. CI only pushes signed images and opens PRs. No prod credentials in CI
scores.rationale: Claims about OIDC federation, keyless cosign/SLSA, admission policy audit-vs-enforce modes, Pact contract tests and GitOps break-glass drift write-back are all accurate, including subtle areas like admission HA for rollback.

scores.evidence: A shared build, test, sign and deploy path (golden path) that 50 existing services move onto in waves
scores.rationale: Precisely answers the sequencing request with phases, gates and dependencies, resolves ambiguities as labeled assumptions, and defers scope (Backstage, ephemeral envs) explicitly with triggers.

scores.evidence: The system of record for "what's deployed" is the old pipeline until cutover, then the environment repo
scores.rationale: The trust-boundary, Git-as-only-deploy-path and template decisions are honored consistently across phases, validation and cross-cutting tables, with data ownership (system of record) explicit at every transition.

scores.evidence: Red-team test of 5 attacks: fork PR deploy; CI token writing to the prod cluster or prod environment paths; unsigned or outside image applied
scores.rationale: V0–V6 tie checkable thresholds to specific risks, test the riskiest decision (trust boundary) before exposure, label thresholds ASSUMPTION/UNKNOWN, and continue post-cutover via per-wave scorecards.

scores.evidence: Assumptions this plan rests on. If any is wrong, the phase order changes, so please confirm
scores.rationale: Every design-bearing assumption is explicit with its consequence if wrong, numbers are tagged BASELINE/ASSUMPTION/UNKNOWN with confirmation owners, and missing inputs are listed with when they are needed.

scores.evidence: The platform becomes the way an unreviewed or malicious artifact reaches production across many services
scores.rationale: Supply-chain compromise, fleet-wide template bugs, platform outages and bad deploys get concrete detection and recovery, but rollback-safe database schema migrations and flaky-test erosion are not handled despite rollback being central.

scores.evidence: Self-run components ≤ 3 (Argo CD, policy controller, External Secrets); everything else managed
scores.rationale: On-call paging, delivery dashboards, rehearsed break-glass, game days, DR rebuild test and an explicit operational-complexity cap sized to a stated ~4-person team make operation realistic.

scores.evidence: Replay 2× the measured peak concurrency as synthetic jobs for 2 h; project monthly cost from the bills
scores.rationale: The dominant driver (runner compute) is identified, cost is projected from measured load before fleet commitment, budget is honestly marked UNKNOWN with an owner, and build-vs-buy and showback controls have triggers.

scores.evidence: R3: once exposed, a compromise can't be undone
scores.rationale: Decisions are explicitly classified by reversibility, the R3 trust/secrets choices get the earliest validation, the only irreversible step (deleting old CI) is gated by V6, and every default has a revisit trigger.

scores.evidence: GitHub Actions on GitHub-hosted runners, managed registry, Argo CD. Build only the templates and policy
scores.rationale: Builds only templates and policy on managed tooling, caps self-run components, and defers Backstage, ephemeral environments, merge queues and multi-region behind concrete pull-forward triggers.

scores.evidence: Wave 2 and fleet scale-up. If it fails: ARC self-hosted runners
scores.rationale: A concrete day-zero slice, dependency-justified phase order, numbered tasks, checkable exit gates and pre-decided fallback branches for each failed validation let a team start immediately.

checklist.evidence: Inventory all 50 services: stack, deploy target, secrets, tier, owner... One shared golden path (versioned reusable workflows plus Argo CD), with a documented escape hatch
new pipeline run in shadow next to the old one for 1 week with matching test results... wave 1 = 5 low-criticality services
pushed to the registry by digest... the same digest is promoted by an environment-repo PR; build once, promote the same digest
OIDC from CI to the cloud; remove every long-lived credential... Fork PRs get no secrets
Keyless cosign signing plus SLSA provenance. Admission policy enforced in prod... CODEOWNERS and required reviews on workflow files
Rolling deploy with automatic health checks for all. Argo Rollouts canary with automated analysis for tier-1
checked with consumer-driven contract tests (Pact), not lockstep releases in a shared environment
PR checks run synchronously (≤ 15 min). Long suites run after merge, before prod... No prod data in CI; tests use synthetic data
PR p90 < 15 min... container build with BuildKit and registry cache... lockfile-keyed caches
Hosted runners meet queue time within budget... Replay 2× the measured peak concurrency... project monthly cost from the bills
CI: 99.5% in business hours... Per-service lead time, deploy frequency, failure rate and restore-time dashboards... page the platform on-call
CODEOWNERS on each team's environment-repo paths... break-glass events go to the SIEM... Template repo owned by platform and security
